newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE SHARES END AT NEW 4-YR LOWS, MAY STEADY.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE SHARES END AT NEW 4-YR LOWS, MAY STEADY.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark share index closed at a fresh four-year low on Wednesday after heavy selling of some blue chip stocks, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended at 1,875.38 points, down 18.08 and at its lowest level since August 1993.
"The selling was pretty broad-based," said one local institutional broker. "You are really going against the grain a bit to ask anyone to buy at the moment."
The weakest STII stock was drinks firm Fraser & Neave, which ended 65 cents down at a 54-month low of Singapore $8.90 on the back of a broker's sell recommendation.
Marine-based conglomerates Keppel Corp and SembCorp were 15 cents and 20 cents weaker at S$5.75 and S$6.35 respectively.
But most of the other STII component stocks showed less dramatic falls and some dealers suggested the index was likely to stabilise later in the week.
"I think it will drift sideways, moving plus or minus 20 or 30 points from here," said one dealer. "I don't think we will see 1,800 points on the STII soon."
One of the most active early stocks was compact disc-maker SM Summit, which plunged nearly 38 percent after its offices were raided in connection with software piracy charges.
The stock was suspended after it had dropped 39.5 cents to S$0.655 on volume of more than 12 million shares.

Officials of the Business Software Alliance industry watchdog said SM Summit's offices were raided following civil suits by Microsoft and two other U.S.-listed firms. SM Summit officials were due to hold a news conference at 0930 GMT.
